newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL falls, steals the show on Budapest mkt.
newsitem.headline: MOL falls, steals the show on Budapest mkt.

text.p: Most Hungarian shares closed little changed in modest volumes on Monday as the market received only little help from the Dow's over one percent rise on Friday, traders said.
Modest volumes in most stocks signalled that many investors might have scaled down their activities as they bite nails to see the preliminary 1996 results.
The BUX index finished at 5,596.96 points, down 60.37.

"Generally, lower turnover characterised trading and this is connected to the fact that investors are waiting for the annual reports," said Szabolcs Gyongyosi of Daewoo Securities. "But MOL dominated the day."
Of the total spot share turnover of 3.62 billion, MOL alone accounted for 2.13 billion forints with a volume of almost 700,000 shares.
MOL continued to slide amid selling by investors who hope to buy the stocks back at a lower price during MOL's privatisation, traders said.
"Investors are selling the paper because they think the subscription price will be below current levels in the privatisation," one trader said earlier today.
MOL shares closed at 3,000 forints, down 300.
Tile manufacturer Zalakeramia opened a shade firmer but finally closed slightly lower following a 'buy' recommendation by ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett this morning.
Zalakeramia shares opened at 9,000 forints, up from Friday's close of 8,960 forints, and closed at 8,900.
Regional food wholesaler and retailer Balaton Fuszert remained untraded after news that Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt had decided to sell a 50 percent plus one share stake.
Elsewhere on the market chemicals and pharmaceuticals closed mixed, bank shares drifted lower, while beverages moved moved higher.
Borsodchem firmed 25 forints to 6,125, while TVK fell 115 forints to 2,405.
Richter jumped to a new high of 12,100 forints, before it retreated to close at 11,900, down 100. Egis advanced 50 forints to 11,500, while Human dipped 50 forints to end at 3,150.
Hungarian bourse-listed companies have to submit their annual results to the bourse by February 15.
